props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · progress swept by script
props.title: Reading a Texture

B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab sprite (teal test sprite, scale to fit 640x360), lab-shaders/18-dissolve.gdshader; noise_tex = NoiseTexture2D (FastNoiseLite seed 7, frequency 0.02, 256 x 256: the Lab's 'noise' kind); ramp_tex = GradientTexture1D (#8A2A12, #F08A2C, #F7D46B, 256 wide); `--animate progress:0.05:0,0.97:1` (fractions of the beat), 30 fps, Forward+, scripted sweep (label it). Verified frames: evidence/planning-checks/png/plus-a3-18-dissolve-*.png (sprite 23,512 px whole at 0; 0 px at 1).
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Reading a Texture' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: the teal test sprite sits whole, then burns away from the edges in, a yellow-orange-red rim around every hole, while a thin 0 to 1 strip under the window carries a marker labelled 'progress' that rides from 0 to 1 with the burn.
B01.motion_claim: The sprite burns away as the progress marker rides from 0 to 1.

show.event: the first holes open at the darkest clouds

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a sprite dissolving
B01.why: A real render of the finished effect is the honest promise for the next ten minutes; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: A 6-by-6 grid of cells: the cream letter F on teal (the film's tiny table), with a one-cell teal margin. Beside it a swatch box with four numbers under it, and under the grid an address readout '(u, v)'. A terracotta dot (the address) starts at the top-left cell, a thin line runs from the dot to the swatch, the swatch takes that cell's color and the four numbers fill in (0.98, 0.98, 0.96, 1.0). Labels: 'texture', 'address', 'color'.
B02.motion_claim: The address dot hops from cell to cell and, each time, the swatch changes to that entry's color.

show.event: dot on a cream cell: swatch cream, four numbers
dot on a teal cell: swatch teal (0.37, 0.64, 0.57, 1.0); settles through 60 %
dot on the next cream cell

B02.why: A grid with a moving address and a swatch that answers is the whole idea of a lookup, as motion; a render would show the result but not the asking.

cues.label: fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers
COLOR: the color of the pixel being drawn

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · a ColorRect with no image of its own

B03.capture_spec: C02: Lab rect 360x360 logical, lab-shaders/01-lookup.gdshader, --tex tex=checker, still PNG at 4K. Verified probes: (0.06, 0.06) = (0.980, 0.977, 0.961) cream; (0.19, 0.06) = (0.372, 0.639, 0.569) teal.
B03.visual_intent: Code card at left (the four-line lookup shader); at right a real Godot window: a plain Color Rect that now shows the 8-by-8 teal and cream checker picture. A terracotta ring moves to one cream cell and then one teal cell, each with its address as a readout.
B03.motion_claim: The ring hops to a cell, and its address and color are read out.

show.event: fragment line highlighted with its meaning
COLOR defined on the lookup line
ring on a cream cell, address (0.06, 0.06)
ring on a teal cell, address (0.19, 0.06)

B03.why: Code and its result side by side is the claim: one line fills the whole shape from a table the shape never owned.

cues.label: uniform: a value your game sets from outside
sampler2D: the type of a texture a shader reads

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · same shader, three tables, switched by script

B04.capture_spec: C03: three Lab stills of lab-shaders/01-lookup.gdshader on a 360x360 rect, joined with ffmpeg, one third of the clip each: tex = tiny_f (the 6x6 F, default filter: smeared), gradient, noise (Lab kinds). Verified: F centre probes (0.25, 0.25) cream, (0.0833, 0.0833) teal; the F at (0.15, 0.25) blends to (0.608, 0.769, 0.722).
B04.visual_intent: Code card at left with the uniform line highlighted. At right the same real Godot window shows three tables in turn with no change to the code: the small cream F on teal (smeared, because it is tiny), the red-green gradient, the grey noise. A caption under the window says 'same code'.
B04.motion_claim: The window's picture changes from table to table while the code stays put.
B04.runner_up: manim: a slot with three tables plugging in
B04.why: Three real renders of one unchanged shader are the proof that the table is the variable; the drawing would only say so.

cues.label: filter_nearest: a hint; reads the closest entry only

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · two renders of the same table

B05.capture_spec: C04: two Lab renders of the 6x6 F table on 360x360 rects, side by side (ffmpeg hstack): left lab-shaders/01-lookup.gdshader, right lab-shaders/02-nearest.gdshader; right panel revealed at 40 % of the beat. Verified at (0.15, 0.25): linear (0.608, 0.769, 0.722) blend, nearest (0.372, 0.639, 0.569) the closest entry.
B05.visual_intent: Code card at left with the hint highlighted. At right two real panels of the small F table side by side: on the left the smeared default, on the right the crisp blocks after the hint. Panel labels 'default' and 'filter_nearest'.
B05.motion_claim: The right panel snaps from smeared to crisp blocks next to the unchanged left one.

show.event: right panel appears: crisp blocks, labelled filter_nearest

B05.runner_up: ShaderLab with one panel and a toggle
B05.why: A smeared F beside a crisp F is the whole difference; the voice points at the left, then the right.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · same table, new address

B06.capture_spec: C05: two Lab renders of the F table (filter_nearest) on 360x360 rects, hstack: left lab-shaders/02-nearest.gdshader, right lab-shaders/03-flip.gdshader; right panel revealed at 40 %. Verified: stem texel (0.25, 0.4167) cream in the original and teal when flipped; (0.75, 0.4167) teal in the original and cream when flipped.
B06.visual_intent: Code card at left with the address line highlighted. At right two real panels: the F table as it is, then, beside it, the same table flipped left to right (the F's stem moves from left to right). Labels 'same table' and 'new address'.
B06.motion_claim: The F's stem jumps from the left side to the right side as the new address is applied.

show.event: right panel appears: the F flipped, labelled new address

B06.why: A real flipped F next to the original is the evidence that the lookup, not the table, changed.

cues.label: repeat_enable: a hint; the table starts over

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · two renders, UV times two

B07.capture_spec: C06: two Lab renders of the F table on 360x360 rects, hstack: left lab-shaders/04-repeat-off.gdshader (revealed at 25 %), right lab-shaders/05-repeat-on.gdshader (revealed at 65 %). Verified probes (0.625, 0.2083) and (0.125, 0.625): repeat off = teal, teal; repeat on = cream, cream.
B07.visual_intent: Code card at left (repeat enable). At right two real panels of the F table asked for twice the address: on the left with repeat disabled a half-size F in the top-left corner with the edge entries smeared out to the right and downward; on the right with repeat enabled a two-by-two tiling of F. Labels 'repeat_disable' and 'repeat_enable'.
B07.motion_claim: The left panel streaks outward; the right panel tiles.

show.event: left panel appears, labelled repeat_disable: edges stretched
right panel appears, labelled repeat_enable: four tiles

B07.runner_up: manim: a table with an arrow running off its edge
B07.why: Streaks beside tiles show both settings at once; a diagram would need to explain what the render simply shows.
